slides.title: One word. *Three lessons.*
slides.sub: A teacher said just one sound. Three students heard three different things.

slides.title: The class that got *one word*
slides.body: In the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, gods, humans and demons study with Prajapati, the creator. At the end they ask: "Teach us." He says only: "Da."

slides.title: Gods heard: *Control yourself*
slides.body: Damyata means hold yourself back. The gods had everything, so their trap was wanting more. Try it: before you reply in anger, wait 10 seconds.

slides.title: Humans heard: *Give*
slides.body: Datta means give. We keep things for ourselves: money, time, praise. Try it: this week, give one thing for no reason. A meal, an hour, a kind word.

slides.title: Demons heard: *Be kind*
slides.body: Dayadhvam means be kind. The demons' trap was being harsh. Try it: when someone messes up, ask "Are you okay?" before you point it out.

slides.deva: तदेतदेवैषा दैवी वागनुवदति स्तनयित्नुर्द द द इति दम्यत दत्त दयध्वमिति । तदेतत्त्रयं शिक्षेद्दमं दानं दयामिति ॥
slides.iast: tad etad evaiṣā daivī vāg anuvadati stanayitnur da da da iti, damyata datta dayadhvam iti; tad etat trayaṃ śikṣed damaṃ dānaṃ dayām iti
slides.meaning: The divine voice of thunder repeats it: "Da! Da! Da!" Control yourself, give, be kind. So learn these three.

slides.title: Same word. *Right answer* for each.
slides.body: The text says Prajapati told all three: "Yes, you understood." Tradition holds we have all three inside us. Screenshot this: Control. Give. Be kind.

slides.title: Which *Da* do you need this week?
slides.sub: Save this for your next hard day, and send it to the friend who needs one of the three. Follow @sutraverselife for daily life lessons from ancient wisdom.
